item.title: The Death of Design Patterns
item.description:
Every now and then, I see Design Patterns floated as a kind of next-step resource for programmers after they’ve gotten comfortable with a language, typically an object-oriented (or at least object-aware) one. I don’t particularly have a problem with OOP as a concept, though I agree with its critics that inheritance is overused in teaching materials by several orders of magnitude.

But as for Design Patterns itself, I personally think these days that it only serves as a window into 90s programming philosophy - a historical relic of a bygone age, and one that I’m not all that interested in revisiting (unlike my passion for Software Tools from the 70s).
